\subsection{Replicate variance on the ablation grid}
\label{sec:tier-noise}

We ran the leave-one-out ablation over three model tiers on
\textsc{subset20b}, a 20-task split of LakeQA stratified jointly on node
count and historical solve rate. Every axis is held at the oracle and one
axis is degraded per cell, giving seven cells per model. Each cell was run
\textbf{three times} under identical configuration, so every number carries
a standard deviation rather than resting on a single sample.

That replication is the central result. The mean per-cell standard
deviation is 6.5\,pp, so a two-sigma interval spans
$\pm13$\,pp and an effect must exceed roughly 13\,pp to be
distinguishable from run-to-run variance. Since one task is worth 5\,pp at
$n=20$, that threshold is about 3 tasks.

Of the 24 degraded cells, only
7 clear that threshold: Search: BM25 at \texttt{gpt-5.4-nano} ($-23.3$\,pp), Plan: Default at \texttt{gpt-5.2} ($-21.7$\,pp), Search: PNEUMA at \texttt{gpt-5-mini} ($-16.7$\,pp), Search: BM25 at \texttt{gpt-5.2} ($-16.7$\,pp), Search: BM25 at \texttt{gpt-5-mini} ($-15.0$\,pp).
The search axis is the one effect that replicates across every tier;
the remaining cells cannot be separated from noise at this sample size.

The reference cells themselves are \texttt{gpt-5.4-nano} 36.7\% ($\sigma=2.9$), \texttt{gpt-5-mini} 68.3\% ($\sigma=2.9$), \texttt{gpt-5.2} 68.3\% ($\sigma=7.6$), \texttt{gpt-5.6-luna} 65.0\%.
\texttt{gpt-5-mini} and \texttt{gpt-5.2} land on the same mean
(68.3\%), despite a roughly sevenfold difference in
price per token.
On this split the frontier model does not outperform the smaller
one, and a single round would have suggested otherwise: round~1
alone put \texttt{gpt-5.2} 5\,pp below \texttt{gpt-5-mini}.
